title: 1995 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In the figure, \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) are diameters of the circle with center \(O,\) \(\overline{AB}\perp\overline{CD},\) and chord \(\overline{DF}\) intersects \(\overline{AB}\) at \(E.\) If \(DE=6\) and \(EF=2,\) then the area of the circle is

solutions.text: Let the radius be \(r\) and \(OE=x.\) Intersecting chords gives \[ (r+x)(r-x)=6\cdot2, \] so \(r^2-x^2=12.\) Put \(O=(0,0),\) \(D=(0,-r),\) and \(E=(x,0).\) Since \(DE:EF=3:1,\) \[ \begin{aligned} F&=D+\frac43(E-D)\\ &=\left(\frac{4x}{3},\frac r3\right). \end{aligned} \] Because \(F\) lies on the circle, \(\frac{16x^2}{9}+\frac{r^2}{9}=r^2,\) so \(r^2=2x^2.\) Therefore \(x^2=12\) and \(r^2=24.\) The area is \(24\pi,\) so the correct answer is C.
hints: Place \(O\) at the origin and express \(F\) using the fact that \(E\) divides \(\overline{DF}\) in a \(3:1\) ratio
